data.title: Freckles (ephelides) — viva
data.summary: Pigmentary disorders · 6 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Freckles (ephelides)** (Pigmentary disorders)_

**Q1. What are freckles?**
- Small (1–5 mm) light-brown, well-defined macules on sun-exposed skin (face, arms, shoulders) of fair-skinned people (Fitzpatrick I–II), appearing in early childhood (2–4 y), darkening in summer and fading in winter

**Q2. Genetics and pathogenesis.**
- MC1R variants (red hair colour phenotype — red hair, fair skin), IRF4, ASIP; UV-induced increase in melanin synthesis and transfer by a normal number of melanocytes (increased activity, larger melanosomes)
- Marker of UV sensitivity and higher melanoma/NMSC risk

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Increased melanin in basal keratinocytes; melanocyte number normal (sometimes fewer but larger), no elongation of rete ridges — unlike lentigo

**Q4. Differentiate freckle from lentigo simplex and solar lentigo.**
- Freckle: sun-dependent darkening, fades in winter, normal melanocyte number, no rete elongation, childhood, fair skin
- Lentigo simplex: not sun-dependent, any site incl. mucosa, does not fade, increased melanocytes along elongated rete ridges
- Solar lentigo: older adults, chronic sun damage, larger, persistent, elongated club-shaped pigmented rete

**Q5. Syndromic freckling.**
- Axillary/inguinal freckling — NF1 (Crowe's sign), Legius syndrome
- Xeroderma pigmentosum — early, severe freckling and poikiloderma in sun-exposed skin of infants
- Centrofacial lentiginosis, Peutz–Jeghers (lentigines, not freckles)

**Q6. Management.**
- Reassurance; photoprotection (sunscreen, hats); cosmetic — Q-switched/picosecond lasers (532 nm), IPL, cryotherapy, depigmenting creams; recurrence with sun exposure
- Skin cancer awareness and self-examination in people with many freckles

## Quick spotter facts
- Small brown macules that darken in summer and fade in winter — freckles; normal melanocyte count

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Melanocytic macules). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
